Large terrestrial vertebrates would be least affected initially owing to their ability to leave the area. Small mammals, amphibians, some reptiles, and many invertebrates within the reservoir area would be eliminated or suffer significant impacts from construction operations. Young birds, especially altricial forms, would experience similar impacts should construction begin late in the spring or during the early summer. Construction impacts would be particularly severe to cold-blooded forms should work in the impoundment area commence during the winter season, disturbing major wintering areas.
Deer population indices presented in Subsection 2.2.2 indicate a huntable population that is increasing. If the whitetail deer population in nearby areas has not reached the carrying capacity of the habitat, the displaced deer would be expected to seek out other available areas. Overall, the area's long-term capacity to sustain deer would be reduced at least by an area equivalent to the fenced periphery of the impoundment site. Turkey would be expected to move from the impoundment site, and the area would cease to be of significance to black bear, feral pig, and many other game as well as non-game species.
The FPC Staff is uncertain as to the exact impact of the proposed action upon populations of endangered species. It is unlikely that the area currently contributes directly to the sustenance of the peregrine falcon or the southern bald eagle. In times past, the region provided food and cover to wide-ranging cougar, and may still contribute these wildlife benefits to an unknown degree. With the exception of osprey, predatory bird species listed as undetermined and described in Subsection 2.2.3. could benefit from exposure of prey species deprived of natural escape cover during early stages of reservoir construction. Such benefits would only be temporary, however.
Any populations of a surviving stream fauna within the proposed impoundment area would be meager in view of vegetation clearing and land moving activities proposed. Similar conclusions apply to local populations of reptiles. Construction impacts could eliminate some southern populations of the green salamander and may also affect the spring salamander and Jordan's salamander as described in Subsection 2.2.3.
